title: White Pizza with Cheese, Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: White pizza with cheese and a thick crust is a classic Italian pizza without tomato sauce, topped with a generous layer of mozzarella, parmesan, and sometimes ricotta. The dough is made from flour, water, yeast, and salt, then shaped into a thick, soft yet crispy crust that holds the aromatic cheese blend.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional “white” pizza originated in Naples as an alternative to tomato‑based pies when tomatoes were seasonal.
The cheese blend often combines several varieties to achieve a more complex flavor and texture.
A thick crust requires a longer bake, resulting in a puffier interior and a crunchy exterior.
Some regions add garlic, olive oil, and herbs (oregano, basil) to enhance the aroma.
White pizza is usually served without additional sauces, letting the cheese shine.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheeses used are rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Mozzarella and parmesan provide complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamin B12 content
items.content: Dairy cheeses supply vitamin B12, supporting nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic potential (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Certain aged cheeses, like parmesan, may contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of a thick crust and cheese delivers lasting fullness, helping to curb snacking.

items.title: High calorie count
items.content: The thick dough and abundant cheese make this pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheeses contain saturated fats, which can affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may need lactose‑free cheeses or alternatives.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the white pizza hot, sliced into individual portions. Fresh arugula, shaved parmesan, or a drizzle of balsamic glaze add a bright contrast. It can be eaten with hands or with a knife and fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.
